description:
Filed s520a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18), the residue of #3404.  A chained `my` whose final initializer holds a declarator at its OWN level still refuses the whole file ("Parser2 TODO: self-referential init"), though perl runs it:
    my @a = (my @b = (1,2)); print "@a|@b\n"; my @c = my @d = (3, my $q = 4); print "@c|@d|$q\n";
perl 5.40.3: `1 2|1 2` / `3 4|3 4|4`.  PCL (s520a tree): Transpile failed at the second statement (Parser2 `_elems_declare_at_level` answers true for `my $q` at the initializer's level, by design of #3404 -- the refusal was kept, not widened).  LOUD, not silent.  Fix shape: the chained path could lower the inner declaration first (its own `p-let`) and then the chain, as perl's left-to-right evaluation does; the self-reference that actually needs the refusal is a READ of a name the same chain declares (`my @a = my @b = (@a)`).  Low: no census row known; Type-Tiny's shape was the nested one.


=== DONE (s521d, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18; commit e5940456) === The inner `my` is an expression-embedded `my` that #3431's let (_decl_init_embedded_my_names / _embedded_my_let) already binds around the whole declaration; the chain arm now refuses only what that let did not take (a name the statement mentions again = a real self-reference, a vetoed / promoted name) and our / local / state at that level (_elems_declare_at_level gains a words-parameterised twin, one body).  Probes pr/chain.pl (5 shapes incl. list heads, a leading inner my, a hash, inside a sub) = perl; `my @a = my @b = (@a, 3)` (perl reads the OUTER @a) still refuses LOUDLY.  Guards Pl/t/parser2-02.t 167-169 (167-168 FAIL on 68aeebf5; 169 = the old INVERSE re-pointed at the read-self-reference, s377).
subject: a chained my whose initializer declares at its OWN level (my @c = my @d = (3, my $q = 4)) still refuses the file; perl runs it (#3404 residue, loud)
